figures.notes: First temporary alternate channel (Sollers Point, NE side): 11 ft depth, 264 ft horizontal, 95 ft vertical clearance, daylight/COTP-discretion only. First transit 1 Apr: tug Crystal Coast pushing a DoD fuel barge. Depths corroborated by USCG MSIB 039-24 (4 Apr 2024).

figures.name: phase_fort_carroll_channel
figures.source_name: Key Bridge Response Unified Command via Marine Log (20 Apr 2024)
figures.notes: Third channel: Fort Carroll Temporary Alternate Channel, 20 ft depth, 300 ft horizontal, 135 ft vertical clearance; USCG Capt. O'Connell estimated it facilitated ~15% of pre-collapse commercial activity. Buoy-laying video dated 19 Apr 2024; announced 19 Apr.

figures.name: phase_limited_access_channel_35ft
figures.unit: date opened (Fort McHenry Limited Access Channel)
figures.source_name: USACE / Key Bridge Response via MarineLink (25 Apr 2024)
figures.notes: Fourth channel: Fort McHenry LAC, controlling depth at least 35 ft, 300 ft horizontal, 214 ft vertical clearance. First transit: bulk carrier Balsa 94 (departing). First inbound container ship MSC Passion III arrived 28 Apr (~1,000 containers, Seagirt). LAC closed ~29 Apr-10 May for Dali wreckage work. NOTE on the '38-ft channel' figure: AP reporting via FTZine states Coast Guard officials put the channel's actual depth at 38 ft while vessels used the 35-ft draft/controlling figure — same channel, not a separate phase.

figures.name: phase_dali_removed_channel_400x50

figures.notes: USACE: 'salvage crews expanded the Port of Baltimore limited access channel to a width of 400 feet and a depth of 50 feet on May 20' with the removal of M/V Dali (refloated a week after the 13 May controlled demolition of the truss section pinning it), 'allowing for the transit of all deep-draft commercial vessels'. USACE full-restoration release dates the widening's effect to 21 May ('widened the Limited Access Channel to 400 feet May 21, permitting all pre-collapse, deep-draft commercial vessels').

derived.method: Computed from the saved verbatim PortWatch rows in this folder. Means are arithmetic means of the daily 'portcalls' field (total vessel calls, all classes incl. non-cargo) over every served row in the window; rows counted as served, including PortWatch zero-activity/imputed rows. Windows per task spec.
derived.virginia_note: No portname 'Virginia' exists in Daily_Ports_Data (LIKE '%Virginia%' returns zero distinct ports). The Port of Virginia complex is served as 'Norfolk' (port826); the repo join input data/graph/portwatch_join_input.json maps graph node sea_virginia -> port826 'Norfolk' (LOCODE US ORF). Filter was by portname/portid, NOT by LOCODE.
derived.baltimore_closure_note: Closure-window mean is NOT zero: 62 of 75 days show >0 calls, totalling 161 calls, dominated by roro (66), dry_bulk (44), general_cargo (22), tanker (13); container calls nearly vanish (16 total, 0.21/day vs 1.60/day baseline). This residual is consistent with terminals seaward of the bridge (e.g. Sparrows Point/Tradepoint Atlantic) plus the phased alternate channels — the main Fort McHenry channel was blocked, the port polygon was not hermetically sealed. 2024-03-26 itself serves portcalls=0.
derived.baltimore_recovery_note: 7-day trailing mean on 2024-06-23 = 4.857 calls/day, first date after 2024-06-10 at/above the 4.8375 threshold. Trailing means 2024-06-11..06-22 ranged 3.857-4.714 (all below threshold).
derived.virginia_note_stats: Virginia/Norfolk CALL counts are flat (+2.08%) across the closure window while PortWatch-estimated IMPORT tonnage rises +28.6% — diversion shows up as fuller/larger ships and cargo mix, not more calls, in this layer.
